executiveSummary: Law enforcement, platforms, and election bodies undertook significant actions this period. The Manhattan District Attorney seized 12 domains tied to large-scale non-consensual deepfake sexual imagery (reportedly impacting more than 1,200 victims), marking a major crackdown on industrialized deepfake abuse. View Article Election-related risks are rising. Independent testing highlighted that major AI tools can still be maneuvered to generate false election content for the U.S. midterms, underscoring real-time misuse pathways. Source Separately, Brazil's top electoral court formalized deepfake definitions for political advertising ahead of October voting, signaling proactive governance. View Article Consumer fraud via voice cloning remains acute. The FBI reported persistent, large-scale impersonation scams with substantial losses, while local authorities in Texas warned of sophisticated emergency-call voice cloning. Security Advisory View Article On defenses and governance, Meta was directed by its Oversight Board to remove harmful deepfakes and bolster safeguards, while standards and provenance advanced through the EU's code of practice and expanded audio watermark verification support. View Article Source Supporting Report Overall, the threat environment is worsening given concurrent criminal exploitation, election disinformation risks, and high-velocity consumer fraud, despite promising advances in policy, platform enforcement, and provenance tooling.
